summary: This is a Docker Compose configuration that sets up a service called 'dood' (Docker-out-of-Docker) running as an unprivileged user. It builds a container with configurable user ID, group ID, and username, mounts the Docker socket to allow container-to-container Docker access, and runs with a TTY attached for interactive use.

explanations.7: This passes a build argument to the Dockerfile; the value comes from an environment variable DOCKER_OS_GROUPID if it exists, otherwise defaults to 1000 (a standard unprivileged user group ID).
explanations.8: Similar to line 7, but for the user ID—this allows the container to run as a specific user ID rather than root.
explanations.9: This passes the username for the unprivileged user; it defaults to 'johndoe' if the environment variable isn't set.
explanations.10: This sets which user account the container runs as, using the same ID variables from the build arguments so the user inside matches the one we configured.
explanations.13: This mounts the host machine's Docker socket into the container, allowing the container to communicate with and control Docker on the host system.
